title: AMIHOPE LL, Ajinomoto, E-200729
read: 2-page PDF text; page 1 rendered and visually checked
observed: N-epsilon-lauroyl-L-lysine, CAS52315-75-0; flat hexagonal morphology 10–20 um; specific gravity 1.2; insoluble in water/oil; no melting or decomposition below 200 C claimed.
limit: Manufacturer data, not ski testing. Friction chart lacks counterface, speed and temperature conditions. Plate thickness and 50 C shear durability unknown. Do not infer ice lattice or environmental safety.

title: US6555708B1, N-epsilon-long chain acyllysine crystals
read: Full public HTML; Table 1, Preparation Example 1, Experimental Example 2 checked
observed: Powders held on adhesive tape and tested with 50g silicone rubber probe; categorical friction below .25 vs above .35 for mechanically pulverized comparisons. Laboratory recrystallization includes heated dissolution, solvent and neutralization.
limit: No PE ski, 50C or speed equivalence; interval outcomes, not exact coefficients. Shape and preparation co-vary. Prior technical disclosure, no patentability or legal-status assessment.

title: Okubo et al. Tribological properties of 100% cellulose nanofiber (CNF) molding under dry- and boundary lubrication-conditions at CNF/steel contacts (2023)
read: Full publisher HTML; dry friction results, counterface and Raman discussion; Table 1 standalone not retrieved
observed: CNF/steel final dry coefficients about .13 at25C, .24 at50C, .7–.8 at80C; crystalline structure is not enough for low friction.
limit: SUJ2 steel rather than PE. Do not substitute load/speed from a related study whose table was accessible. Raman ratio decrease is not direct absolute bulk crystallinity.

title: Okubo et al. Novel Environmentally Superior Tribomaterial with Superlow Friction: 100% Cellulose Nanofiber Molding (2023)
read: Full publisher HTML, methods and friction results
observed: Low coefficients near .01–.02 used PAO oil with 1 wt% glycerin monooleate at50C; speed dependence studied.
limit: Oil-lubricated results excluded as proof of dry, oil-free project performance.

type: expert safety assessment, not independent raw trial data
title: CIR Safety Assessment of Amino Acid Alkyl Amides as Used in Cosmetics, final2013
read: PDF pp4–5 and Table9 p40; conclusions and inhalation discussion
observed: Lauroyl lysine cosmetic formulations supported non-irritating cosmetic use; assessment identifies no inhalation data and reasons from cosmetic exposure scenarios.
limit: Does not validate ski abrasion dust, outdoor release, eye impact, chronic occupational exposure, winter water quality, or our carrier/binder. Underlying lauroyl lysine human formulation data include unpublished industry submissions.
